decisive_items: segmental erythema and ulceration in the descending and sigmoid colon
subepithelial edema, hemorrhage, mild crypt architectural distortion, and an acute inflammatory infiltrate without granulomas or dysplasia
mild thickening of the mid- and distal descending colon with adjacent inflammatory stranding
response.rationale: Young woman on a progestin-only contraceptive with subacute bloody diarrhea, segmental left colon involvement with rectal sparing, and biopsy showing submucosal edema/hemorrhage with acute inflammation is most consistent with ischemic colitis.

rejected.why: IBD is less likely given the acute hemorrhagic/edematous biopsy pattern, segmental left colon distribution, and lack of granulomas or more definitive chronic changes.
CT explicitly shows no diverticulosis, and there is no perforation or abscess; bloody diarrhea and biopsy findings are not diverticular.
Stool assays for Clostridioides difficile toxins were negative.
Microscopic colitis typically causes non-bloody watery diarrhea with normal endoscopy, not segmental ulceration and hemorrhage.
Three-week duration, negative stool cultures, segmental ulceration, and markedly elevated calprotectin argue against acute gastroenteritis.
Colitis is too nonspecific; the clinical, endoscopic, and biopsy features identify ischemic colitis as the specific type.
